newsitem.title: USA: Ford sales dip 4.3 percent on slower truck sales.
newsitem.headline: Ford sales dip 4.3 percent on slower truck sales.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. reported Monday that its U.S. light vehicle sales fell 4.3 percent in April, a larger drop than analysts expected as light truck sales rose a scant 0.5 percent because of shipping problems.

Ford, the nation's No. 2 automaker, sold 318,392 light vehicles in April, down from 332,777 a year ago. Car sales fell 10.7 percent to 130,175. Light trucks, the segment that includes pickup trucks, minivans and sport utilty vehicles, rose to 188,217 from 187,034.
Ford blamed the slight rise in its truck sales on a shortage of rail cars used to move new vehicles.

"Our dealers could have delivered even more trucks to their customers in April were it not for a shortage of bi-level rail cars to transport new trucks," said Bob Rewey, Ford's group vice president of marketing and sales.

Rewey said the Windstar minivan was most affected, although he said sales of Explorer sport utility vehicles and F-Series pickup trucks were also hurt. The problem is likely to continue through the second quarter, when truck output is at its peak levels, he said.
"We're looking at every possible alternative to expedite shipments and address the shortages that we know are frustrating to prospective owners and to our dealers," he said.
Ford was the last of the Big Three to report its April sales. General Motors Corp. last week reported a 5.4 percent drop in sales to 413,443. Chrysler Corp.'s sales tumbled 11.5 percent to 204,080.

Ford, which has some of the hottest selling pickup truck and sport utility vehicles on the market, said it increased its North American second quarter truck production forecast by 10,000 units to 750,000.
"That's an increase of 74,000 trucks or 11 percent over the second quarter of 1996," said Rewey. "We're making every effort to build what our consumers want."

Meanwhile, Ford said it has received more than 9,000 dealer orders for its new Lincoln Navigator full-size sport utility vehicle. The Navigator, a luxury version of the Ford Expedition, is due to go on sale July 1.
